newsitem.title: FRANCE: Union calls day of protest in sugar industry.
newsitem.headline: Union calls day of protest in sugar industry.

text.p: A French trade union has called a protest on September 11 against plans by sugar cooperative Union des Sucreries et Distilleries Agricoles (SDA) to close its Berneuil and Maizy plants in northern France.
Berniere is scheduled to close in 1997 and Maizy by the year 2000.

The agro-Food branch of the CFDT union said in a statement the break-up of France's number three sugar producer Compagnie Francaise de Sucrerie (CFS) was paving the way for an in-depth restructuring of the French sugar industry.
In June Eridania Beghin-Say agreed to acquire CFS and later resell 52 percent of CFS's assets and sugar quotas to Generale Sucriere and to a group of French sugar cooperatives.
The transaction is to take place when the sugar harvest is completed at the end of November.
CFS produces 300,000 tonnes of sugar annually at five refineries and employs over 800 people.
Analysts have said the deal offers sugar producers opportunities to secure additional quotas and rationalise operations before the European Union's sugar marketing system expires in 2001.

Based on geographical locations, the most likely scenario is that Eridania will keep two plants, Vauciennes and Villenoy, and sell the Marle plant to Generale Sucriere, the Bucy Le Long plant to SDA and the Bray plant to Sucre-Union, a group of coperatives, industry sources have said.
The acquisition of the Bucy plant was expected to lead SDA to close the neighbouring plants of Maizy and Berneuil. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
